title: The Inspection Report That Led Theranos to Void Two Years of Tests
conflicts: Voided results: in May 2016 Theranos told CMS (per the WSJ, via Reuters/NBC and TechCrunch) it had voided all 2014-15 Edison results and sent tens of thousands of corrected reports; in June 2016 a spokesperson told Bloomberg (via BioPharma Dive, California Healthline) under 1% of all its results were voided or corrected. Both are given with who said them and when. A Walgreens figure of about 31,000 affected customers is only in sources that block the checker and is not used. CMS letter dated January 2016 (CNBC, Fortune) vs February (BioPharma Dive); January used.
notes: Episode moved from the 2018 dissolution to the 2016 response to the CMS inspection, because Holmes had been replaced as CEO by David Taylor in June 2018 and he announced the dissolution; the dissolution, SEC settlement, verdict, sentence and 2025 appeal are given as aftermath. Built on the Ninth Circuit's 2025 opinion (Das testimony, voiding, verdict by count), the SEC's 2018 release and major reporting; no characterisation of intent beyond the verdict. The Ninth Circuit PDF loads but the checker cannot read its text, so it shows as live without a name match. Quote stance is affirms (on the work of verification), not on Holmes's choices.
